sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: SDS-PAGE under reducing and non-reducing conditions in K562 cells confirmed expression and correct oligomerization of the tagged construct (PMC10330345, Supplemental Figure 1). Functional assays for γδ T-cell activation were performed with these constructs. NOT MEASURED whether the His tag itself alters function relative to untagged BTN2A1.
sites.rationale: BTN2A1 is a type I transmembrane protein with a 28-residue signal peptide; the sole extracellular N-terminus is the mature chain starting at Q29. An N-terminal tag fused before residue 1 would be cleaved with the signal peptide and lost, so the 6xHis tag in '6xHis-BTN2A1' must be positioned after SP cleavage, i.e., insert_after_residue=28. This is the only extracellular terminus available, making the junction topology-derived. The extracellular domain spans 220 residues (29–248), placing this tag far from the TM boundary. Full-length BTN2A1 with an N-terminal 6xHis tag (6xHis-BTN2A1) cloned into pcDNA3.1(+) and expressed in K562 cells (PMC10330345). BTN2A1 is a type I single-pass TM protein with signal peptide 1–28; the only extracellular N-terminus is the mature chain beginning at residue 29. A tag prepended before residue 1 would be co-translocated with and cleaved off by the signal peptide, so the 6xHis tag must sit after the SP cleavage site (after residue 28) to be retained and detectable. Python-verified: res(28)=A, res(29)=Q; TM boundary at 249 is 220 residues away.

sources.claim: We previously described cloning of full length BTN2A1 containing a C-terminal Myc tag (BTN2A1-myc) or an N-terminal 6x His tag (6xHis-BTN2A1) into pcDNA3.1 (+), as well as the mut1, mut2, L318G, W320A, and L325G mutations on both templates ( 17 ).

literature_notes: L1 (Myc, C-terminal via reverse primer) and L4/L5 (Flag/affinity tags at C-terminus) all place tags at residue 527, which is intracellular (topology 270–527); these are recorded in other_positions. L3 corroborates expression of the L2 constructs in K562 cells but adds no new position. L6 (BTN2A1-NL, NanoLuciferase) uses the naming convention 'BTN2A1-NL' consistent with a C-terminal fusion; the BRET assay with surface Halo589 ligand confirms surface expression of the BTN complex but does not require NL itself to be extracellular — intracellular NL (C-terminal) can still report proximity to an intracellular HaloTag on BTN3A1. Because the clip does not specify the NL junction and the naming convention points to C-terminal (intracellular), L6 does not qualify as an independent extracellular site and is grouped with the other C-terminal intracellular entries. The N-terminal 6xHis site (L2) is classified topology_derived because the paper names no specific residue; the junction is uniquely determined by the signal-peptide boundary.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal Myc tag inserted before the stop codon via reverse primer on full-length BTN2A1; residue 527 (L) is intracellular (topology 270–527).
Flag tag (MDYKDDDDK) inserted at the C-terminus of full-length BTN2A1 to facilitate purification; residue 527 is intracellular.
BTN2A1-NL (NanoLuciferase) construct used in BRET assay; naming convention and intracellular C-terminus topology indicate NL is at residue 527 (intracellular), not on the extracellular face.
